system_summary.NAME: EVOLVED_WORKFLOW_MANAGEMENT_COMPOSED_SYSTEM
system_summary.PURPOSE: Coordinate work whose control, data, resources, commitments and external effects must remain intelligible through ordinary execution, exception, recovery and justified change.
system_summary.ENVIRONMENT: Human and application work may be concurrent, repeated, long-lived, fallible, partly observed and divided among autonomous participants.
CORE_DISTINCTIONS: definition / instance / work item / external object / recorded event
request / receipt / commitment / performance declaration / acceptance
local termination / residual obligation / external outcome
durable replay / valid current meaning / authorised revision
system_summary.OPERATION: Participants exchange requests, offers, data, declarations and acknowledgements; authorised actors perform work on real objects; observations qualify state, effect and acceptance claims. Exception, recovery and revision loops can interrupt ordinary work.
system_summary.SMALLEST_COHERENT_FORM: Enough identity, next/completion meaning, accountable action and result/exception evidence for the actual risk; this can be a manual procedure with a shared record.
system_summary.NONCLAIMS: No universal engine, forced serial pipeline, complete world log, perfect compensation, automatic semantic authority or joint empirical validation of this analytical composition.

relation_semantics.REQUIRES: FROM needs the TO obligation(s) in the stated context, not necessarily distinct tools or owners.
relation_semantics.ENABLES: FROM makes the TO capability possible under the stated guard.
relation_semantics.CONSTRAINS: FROM limits the valid operation or justified claim of TO.
relation_semantics.PROVIDES_EVIDENCE_FOR: FROM supplies bounded evidence consumed by TO; not automatic proof.
relation_semantics.COMMUNICATES_TO: FROM produces a message/declaration interpreted by TO.
relation_semantics.ACTS_THROUGH: FROM is operated through TO mechanisms in the named context.
relation_semantics.FEEDBACK_TO: FROM informs an independently authorised revision of TO; no implicit self-authorisation.
relation_semantics.ALTERNATIVE_TO: Conditional substitutes or alternative configurations, not unconditional equivalence.
relation_semantics.CONFLICTS_WITH: Requirements or claims cannot all be satisfied under the stated assumptions without a discriminating decision.
relation_semantics.REFINES: FROM adds an explicitly narrower/differentiated form to TO.
relation_semantics.SUPERSEDES: FROM is a stronger conditional replacement for the overclaim at TO.
relation_semantics.SHARES_ANCESTRY_WITH: A documented common method/problem does not establish identical semantics or independent evidence.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Messages or events can belong to different cases or attempts.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Referents and data scopes can be distinguished.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: One reused business key is assumed to identify every lifecycle.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Correlation binds an observation to the intended case, message and external object before transition evaluation.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Maintaining aliases and historical bindings has cost and can preserve a wrong match.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Demonstrate binding correctness under duplicates and reused identifiers.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: The selected workflow actually uses the relevant construct.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The declared semantics covers its supported execution context.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Graph layout alone determines all joins, races and termination.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Explicit transition rules give choice, concurrency, repetition and stopping constructs an executable interpretation.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Expressiveness expands verification and operator-understanding burdens.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Test the engine subset rather than requiring every construct.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Enabling predicates depend on shared, scoped or changing data.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Input visibility and freshness policy are declared.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Control readiness implies valid or current inputs.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Binding, access and update rules constrain guard evaluation; data-flow analysis detects selected defects before enactment.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Stronger consistency may block work and still not establish real-world truth.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Specify acceptable staleness and resolve concurrent writes.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Execution needs people, permissions or scarce resources.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Control, data, authority and availability are separate predicates.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A token or role name proves a ready authorised performer.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Control-enabled options are filtered or escalated through eligibility, ownership and capacity decisions.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Joint feasibility can be more expensive than control-flow verification.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Prove only the constraints modelled; gather actual capacity evidence.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A cancelled branch can affect a downstream synchronisation.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Join membership and cancellation scope have defined semantics.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Cancellation supplies the same token as successful completion.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Convergence must account for which activations can still arrive and which have been withdrawn.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Non-local inclusive-join reasoning and race states may grow.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Test cancellation before, during and after arrival.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Multiple instances or repeated activations share a join.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The relevant activation/invocation membership is distinguishable.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Arrivals from different iterations are interchangeable.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Instance thresholds and loop/call scope determine which arrivals count for a particular convergence.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Extra bookkeeping may be unnecessary for safe structured models.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Establish completion thresholds and invocation lifetime.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Competing external events can enable different continuations.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Winner, late-event and timeout rules are explicit.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A race loser cannot already have an outside effect.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Correlate competing arrivals and decide the chosen path without interpreting silence as proof of failure.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Late messages require disposition and may create compensation work.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Define handling of late, duplicate and contradictory events.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Concurrent workers can perform mutually exclusive work.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The enforcement boundary includes the contenders.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A diagrammed critical section locks an external actor automatically.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Claims, leases or other ownership mechanisms realise the exclusion policy for the chosen scope.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Leases may expire while a worker still acts; locking can reduce throughput.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Separate ownership transfer from cancellation of old external effects.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Choosing structured versus general control models.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Required behaviour and available verification technique are known.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: More expressiveness is always better or structure is always adequate.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Model selection limits the semantic fragment to one whose expressive benefit justifies its analysis burden.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Restructuring can duplicate logic or obscure natural interaction.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Compare equivalent behaviour, not merely smaller drawings.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Using a workflow-net verdict to justify enactment.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The selected soundness definition and implementation relation are declared.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Classical soundness proves inevitable progress or external success.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: The meaning of the verdict is bounded by the net class and by correspondence of the enacted subset to that net.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Correspondence evidence and stronger progress reasoning add separate work.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Discharge fairness, resource, time and environment obligations separately.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A selected model is amenable to state analysis or reduction.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The algorithm assumptions match the model.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A reduction preserves unmodelled data, time or participant obligations.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Reachability, reduction or compositional checks establish only their stated behavioural predicate.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: State explosion and abstraction errors can invalidate practical claims.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Record abstraction/reduction conditions and counterexample interpretation.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Import, export or engine replacement is contemplated.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Concrete supported constructs and extensions are identifiable.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A shared file extension or standard badge ensures behavioural portability.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Model-to-engine tests make portability a versioned semantic claim rather than a syntactic assertion.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: A portable subset can exclude useful local functionality.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Recheck actual transformed artefacts and application bindings.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: The practical claim includes progress with scarce resources or deadlines.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Readiness, service time and assignment data can be assessed.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Resource-free net completion entails feasible schedules.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Capacity and timing analysis restrict what a sound control model justifies in the environment.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Predicted service times and calendars can be wrong.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Measure actual availability and escalation effectiveness.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Data-centric or interacting-object coordination is chosen.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Objects, their relationships and data predicates have explicit meaning.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Removing a central sequence removes inter-object dependencies.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Object lifecycle and data availability determine transitions while preserving correlation across interactions.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Distributed object state can make global progress and ownership obscure.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Check coupled object consistency rather than only each lifecycle.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A task is delegated or substituted.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Eligibility, current ownership and applicable duty constraints are preserved.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Delegation transfers any legal or organisational authority automatically.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Reallocate responsibility through the declared lifecycle and re-evaluate constraints for the replacement actor.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Strict constraints can prevent a necessary exception from being resolved.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Name the authority for any explicit constraint waiver.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Duty constraints and available staffing admit no assignment.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The protected separation or binding rule is actually required.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: An unsatisfiable staffing plan can be repaired by silently violating a duty.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Feasibility analysis exposes the conflict so authorised redesign, capacity change or an explicit waiver can be considered.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: More staff, delay or restricted service can be necessary.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: A satisfiable assignment still does not establish a feasible timed schedule.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A human reports work completed.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The report identifies who declared what and for which work item.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Completion click is direct evidence of the intended outside effect.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Work-item state conveys an accountable declaration to a consumer who may accept, inspect or qualify the result.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Additional acceptance steps can add delay and defensive reporting.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Choose proportionate evidence; do not infer need for continuous surveillance.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Commitment and acceptance have distinct consequences.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Participants can distinguish request, undertaking, result declaration and acceptance.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Receipt, acceptance and satisfaction are the same communication act.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Explicit interaction states separate material work from commitments and acceptance claims.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Imposing the full vocabulary on every act can become ceremony.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Acceptance must come from the relevant participant, not the model author.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Situated work cannot be adequately prescribed in advance.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Actors have bounded discretion and access to relevant case information.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Freedom from a route means freedom from accountability.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Participant judgement selects or proposes valid work, deviations and repairs within explicit constraints.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Discretion can introduce inconsistent treatment, hidden work and expertise dependence.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Collect evidence of which freedoms are useful and which need limits.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: An exception or interrupt changes live work.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Affected scope and downstream obligations can be identified.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Stopping local control automatically cancels remote work or fulfils the case.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Handlers classify continuation, suspension, cancellation or escalation and update convergence/closure claims accordingly.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Cancellation races and partially completed work may persist.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Confirm actual termination and residual external obligations.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: An unanticipated deviation requires a repair.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: An authorised actor can assess current state and external consequences.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Editing the definition alone repairs the live case.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Repair either changes valid running state through a checked migration or reconciles the outstanding action without changing the definition.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Repair tools introduce an authority surface and can bypass normal checks.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Maintain reasoned responsibility for exceptional state transitions.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A remote activity times out after it may have committed.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: A timeout reports missing confirmation, not an observed inverse effect.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Timeout proves that no outside action happened.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Uncertainty directs the decision towards safe repetition, status query or reconciliation instead of blind retry.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: The external system may have no query or deduplication interface.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Leave irreducible outcome uncertainty explicit.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Retrying could duplicate a material effect.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Logical operation identity and its effect boundary are specified.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Persisting a workflow step alone makes an arbitrary external action exactly once.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Deduplication, idempotence, an atomic boundary or justified rollback/recovery controls repeat effects; reconcile anything outside that boundary.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Deduplication retention, idempotency design and rollback limits add cost.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Verify the actual cooperating interfaces and key lifetime.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A completed action cannot be rolled back atomically.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: A compensating action is available and separately authorised.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Compensation is an exact inverse of every physical and social consequence.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Forward actions can discharge or modify outstanding obligations while recording irreversible residuals and failures.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Compensation itself can fail and create a further commitment.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Decide whether accepted residuals allow case closure.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Work crosses autonomous participant boundaries.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Each participant controls its own actions and accepts a declared interface.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A global model grants a central engine authority over all parties.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Orchestration exposes one actor’s control; choreography constrains interaction obligations without necessarily creating a controller.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Private constraints and protocol mismatches obstruct global completion.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Establish participant agreement and observable acceptance.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Claiming compatibility or completion of cooperating workflows.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Message identity, delivery and local transition assumptions match the composition model.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Each local process being sound suffices for a sound interaction.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Composition analysis checks coupled send/receive behaviour and the assumptions under which local parts fit.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Unbounded queues and unrestricted models can make analysis difficult.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Do not extend a model proof to unreliable or strategic participants unexamined.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A workflow must survive crashes while coordinating external work.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The retained state can be related to outstanding attempts and outside effects.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A durable engine record is a verified snapshot of every external object.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Recovery reconstructs sufficient instance state, then repeats or reconciles actions under a defined effect policy.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Persistence and reconciliation consume storage, latency and operator effort.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Specify what survives each crash point and what may remain uncertain.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: The engine reconstructs orchestrator state by replay.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Nondeterministic effects are isolated or recorded and code is compatible with history.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Arbitrary I/O or changed branching can be replayed as if deterministic.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Replay consumes durable event history to regenerate the expected command sequence without redoing recorded activities as pure local steps.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Long histories and version constraints complicate evolution.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: State the platform-specific replay contract; other engines can recover differently.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Retention is chosen for recovery and audit consumers.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Required references and deduplication horizons are identified.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: All events must be retained forever or any compact summary is sufficient.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Checkpointing, archival or compaction must preserve the facts needed by outstanding recovery and evidence obligations.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Lossy retention can invalidate deduplication or later interpretation.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Prove the sufficiency of the chosen retained representation for its claim.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Running histories or definitions outlive deployed code versions.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: An old instance remains interpretable by the selected worker/version.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A deployment silently migrates every existing case.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Pinning/coexistence, compatible evolution or checked migration preserve a declared continuity relation.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Supporting old versions costs resources and can preserve old defects.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Define who handles incompatible instances and external references.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A running instance changes its governing process.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Current control, data and outstanding interactions are known well enough to check migration.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Soundness of the target definition is a sufficient migration condition.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: A state transformation maps live work and data to valid target semantics and disposes of unmappable residual obligations.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Migration can require a quiescent point or manual adjudication.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Specify supported change operations and check their concrete preconditions.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: An old definition can safely remain available for its live instances.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Instances can be routed to compatible definitions/workers.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: All instances must immediately use the latest definition.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Definition coexistence avoids risky state transformation while new instances use the revised definition.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Maintaining obsolete code and interactions has cost and risk.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Retire the old version only when its obligations are settled or transferred.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Observed variability indicates a particular kind of flexibility.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The location of uncertainty and authority to resolve it are known.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Adaptive is a single mechanism or every case needs every flexibility mode.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Design alternatives, deviation, underspecification and change select different forms of runtime or design-time freedom.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Combining modes can make responsibility and admissibility less comprehensible.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Classify the actual variation before adding a flexibility mechanism.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Valid behaviour is easier to describe by constraints than a prescribed route.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Constraint semantics, consistency and completion interpretation are explicit.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Constraint permission entails eventual achievement of all goals.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Declarative rules delimit admissible traces while letting performers choose among remaining options.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Constraint interaction and pending obligations can be difficult to understand.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Check dead tasks, satisfiability and progress beyond mere local permission.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Knowledge-intensive work relies on case data and discretionary planning.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Case roles, information access and acceptance criteria are sufficient.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A case-management notation guarantees better decisions or all child tasks succeed.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Data-centred case handling and discretionary task planning support contextual choices without a fully predetermined path.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Guidance and verification may weaken; workers bear decision cost.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Choose hybrids only when the distinction between required and discretionary work remains intelligible.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Recurring exceptional contexts can use tested late-bound subprocesses.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Selection rules and substitute subprocess interfaces have controlled validity.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Reusing a worklet transfers every original precondition to a new context.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Contextual rules select a bounded worklet rather than editing the entire model or repeating an ad hoc repair.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Rule proliferation and context drift can make selection unreliable.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Validate chosen worklet compatibility and retire obsolete rules.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A monitoring or conformance consumer needs engine observations.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Event meaning, case binding and observation scope are known.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Logged transitions describe all actual work or prove its correctness.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Execution histories provide a basis for selected ordering, performance or deviation questions.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Instrumentation can add cost and induce measurement gaming.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Document missing, duplicated and outside events before inference.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A claim crosses from recorded state to actual work or effect.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: There is a declared observable relationship and an appropriate evidence consumer.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A complete engine log is a complete world description.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Observation limits qualify completion, conformance and recovery conclusions and identify when independent effect evidence is needed.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Direct evidence can be costly, intrusive or itself unreliable.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Use task-appropriate sampling or acceptance evidence rather than demanding omniscience.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Measured delay, failure or burden could justify a change in coordination.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Measures have a decision consumer and credible comparison.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A metric improvement automatically authorises process mutation.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Operational and field evidence informs a separate authorised choice to simplify, change or retire a mechanism.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Goodhart effects and confounding can misdirect revision.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Assess distributional effects and preserve a credible counterfactual.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Scientific workflows are shared or re-executed.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Input, code/environment and result identity are interpretable.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A successful process exit means scientific reproducibility or correctness.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Provenance and environment references support a declared reproduction claim that still needs an output/scientific oracle.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Capturing large data and fragile dependencies is costly.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Select exact, statistical or scientific equivalence appropriate to the task.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Scientific work spans distributed compute, data and fallible services.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Task dependency, resource and environment constraints are represented sufficiently.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A scientific DAG proves every workflow is a DAG or removes runtime hazards.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Scheduling and retry mechanisms operate over a domain-specific graph and provenance model.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Data movement, resource heterogeneity and hidden service failure dominate some costs.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Test the stated domain; do not generalise a scheduler benchmark to human coordination.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Low-code templates or engines hide execution and configuration detail.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Actual runtime semantics and extension boundaries can be inspected.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Visual simplicity proves simple runtime behaviour or portability.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Abstraction inspection and semantic tests determine what the visual model does and fails to expose.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Inspecting generated or embedded code reduces some convenience benefits.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Do not infer runtime safety from a static template corpus.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Learned components propose or execute consequential workflow steps.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Permissions, effects, acceptance and semantic dependencies are separately enforced or checked.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: An agent’s plausible plan is authority, verified effect or a replay proof.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Keep model-generated choices inside independently evaluated execution and effect boundaries, with declared fallbacks.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Guarding can be costly and still miss semantic drift or evaluator failure.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: No broad comparative effectiveness or universal safe autonomy is established.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Durable AI work depends on changing retrieval, model or policy context.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: A declared semantic compatibility relation and relevant dependencies are available.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Replaying a stored choice ensures it remains valid in a changed environment.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Proposed semantic-environment binding makes cross-version meaning an explicit recovery concern beyond deterministic command replay. Controlled prototype support discriminates closed-world static pinning from online binding extension when dependencies are discovered during execution.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Dependency capture can be incomplete and compatibility evaluation expensive.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Compatibility contracts are declared, not inferred; independently validate their adequacy. Shared-write and visible-effect serialisability remain outside the demonstrated guarantee.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Claiming generally safe autonomous workflow optimisation.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Safety and improvement criteria could in principle be evaluated.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Static generation results establish general semantic preservation and deployed benefit.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: The broad claim remains unresolved: available recent proposals and template studies do not discharge joint semantic, authority and outcome obligations.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Premature acceptance would automate hidden specification drift.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Need prospective, adversarial and independent comparative deployment evidence.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A terminal case may still have running work, failed effects or unaccepted commitments.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The closure claim states its scope and how residual obligations can be settled or transferred.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A single terminal flag represents all local, external and participant success predicates.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Compose completion, cancellation, acceptance and compensation into explicit accounting for live work and residual obligations; accepted transfer can allow closure.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: A stronger closure account may delay completion or become an unnecessary approval chain.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: The integrated invariant is analytical; each context must choose its actual acceptance and transfer rules.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Recovery or migration spans a change of code, definition or external references.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Old and new references remain interpretable under the chosen continuity claim.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Persistence, replay compatibility and migration correctness are interchangeable.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Preserve a relation between retained instance state, governing semantics and outstanding external actions across recovery or version change.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Cross-version reference maintenance can outlive otherwise retired infrastructure.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: This is a composed interface obligation, not one theorem proved across all cited systems.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: An instance is recovered, migrated or closed with outstanding obligations.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Closure and continuity use the same declared obligation scope.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Migration can erase a residual because its identifier no longer exists in the new model.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Closure accounting constrains which state and references recovery/migration may discard.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Long-lived obligations can prevent aggressive compaction or version retirement.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Define an authorised settlement/transfer rather than retain everything indefinitely.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Evidence of remaining work must survive recovery or migration.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Relevant references retain their meaning.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A rewritten local state alone proves all old effects have been settled.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Continuity makes earlier declarations and external actions available to the present closure decision.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Legacy interpretation and reference resolution impose continuing cost.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Verify the minimum evidence still available after each transformation.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Deciding whether a fuller mechanism earns its place.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: There is an actual risk, consumer or coordination burden.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A retained property entails one tool, artefact or owner per ledger row.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Use the cheapest adequate form, including already adequate manual coordination; add machinery only when it changes a consequential decision or prevents a relevant failure.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Too little structure can conceal rare but severe failures.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Reassess both omission risk and maintenance burden; do not equate cheap with adequate.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A proposed general definition restricts workflows to serial pipelines or DAGs.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The scope includes repeated or interruptible work.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: One finite unfolding captures unbounded recurring operation.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Explicit loops, recursion and cancellation replace the universal DAG restriction while preserving DAGs for genuine acyclic subdomains.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: General models can be harder to analyse.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Use a DAG only with a stated finite/acyclic boundary.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: An exactly-once claim omits the external effect boundary.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Cooperating services and failure assumptions can be stated.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: All observable effects follow from the engine’s durable-state guarantee.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Replace the unqualified claim with a scoped guarantee, tested deduplication/idempotence or explicit reconciliation.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Boundary specification can expose unresolved interfaces.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Do not incorrectly deny valid scoped exactly-once results.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A diagram or standard badge is offered as sufficient correctness.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Actual intended constructs and runtime version are available.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Syntactic validity is behavioural correspondence.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Replace badge-based assurance with relevant model/engine tests and bounded acceptance criteria.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Testing still samples behaviour unless exhaustive under a model.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Retain documents as useful communication, not automatic proof.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A sound new definition is treated as sufficient migration justification.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Running state, old version and outstanding work are known.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Target validity implies a valid mapping from every current state.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Use checked state transformation or explicit version coexistence instead.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Some instances cannot be migrated cheaply or safely.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Identify unsupported current states and select a fallback.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: An audit/conformance claim equates logs with the external world.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Log scope and effect evidence can be separated.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Every relevant action is recorded correctly by the engine.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Replace completeness rhetoric with observation boundaries and appropriate external evidence.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Missing evidence may leave conclusions unresolved.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: State what the record cannot establish.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Compensation is described as universal restoration.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Forward actions and residual harm are distinguishable.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Every act has a reliable, authorised inverse.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Use compensation as a fallible remedial act, preserving irreversible residuals and escalation.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Restitution may not satisfy all parties.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Do not claim equality of original and compensated worlds.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: A product is selected by maximal pattern coverage alone.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Required behaviours and semantic subsets are known.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: More checked catalogue boxes implies better fit.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Choose relevant constructs, integration semantics and cost, rather than universal catalogue compliance.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: A narrow subset can later constrain change.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Technical critique remains partly access-limited; no blanket invalidation of patterns.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Automation is asserted to improve all organisations.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Benefits and costs can be assessed in context.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Adoption or a selected successful case proves causal general benefit.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Use explicit setting, comparison and attrition evidence; retain simpler support or no engine where adequate.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Evaluation costs may be nontrivial for small tasks.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Transfer requires target evidence, not an inherited positive estimate.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: All execution events are proposed for indefinite retention.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Recovery and evidence consumers have identifiable needs.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Storage accumulation itself increases justified assurance.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Retain a sufficient record with defensible compaction, retirement and unresolved-reference handling.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Premature deletion can compromise recovery or evidence.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: No legal retention period is inferred by this research.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Comparing workflow-net verification and declarative progress analysis.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Both analyse possible behaviour under formal transition/trace models.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Shared verification aims make their soundness predicates identical.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: The related verification tradition supplies questions about reachability, dead work and completion, but distinct models retain distinct guarantees.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: False equivalence can transfer the wrong theorem.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Check each predicate and semantic model before reconciliation.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: Comparing scientific and business workflow recovery.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Both coordinate fallible tasks with intermediate state.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: Scientific result validity and business commitment validity are the same.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Shared workflow enactment mechanisms translate into scientific resource/data settings without merging their acceptance or authority models.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Transfer can ignore environmental dependencies and scientific meaning.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Preserve domain-specific assumptions and evidence.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: The completion claim includes a delivered result or participant satisfaction.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: The appropriate consumer and acceptance scope are known.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: One participant’s declaration settles all interpretations of success.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Observed effect and attributable acceptance qualify the instance’s completion claim; they need not be collected as separate forms.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Acceptance disputes or unobservable effects can leave uncertainty.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Avoid requiring impossible certainty; record an explicit evidence standard.

relations.CONTEXT_OR_GUARD: An authorised revision changes definitions, data rules or role constraints.
relations.SHARED_ASSUMPTIONS: Predecessor authority and current-instance continuity obligations remain effective.
relations.INCOMPATIBLE_ASSUMPTIONS: A new rule can authorise its own application retroactively.
relations.COMPOSITION_MECHANISM: Revision changes future enabling and, only under separately checked migration, current instances.
relations.NEW_FAILURE_OR_COST: Self-revision can create circular justification and erase incompatibilities.
relations.UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION: Self-application is a governed context-specific extension, not universal autonomy.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Minimal accountable coordination
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Small stable work with a known responsible participant, simple identity and directly assessable results.
alternative_configurations.FORM: A concise procedure or shared case record with agreed next/completion criteria and an explicit way to handle uncertainty; no engine is mandatory.
alternative_configurations.SUBSTITUTION: A single record may serve several identity/evidence functions when their lifecycles coincide.
alternative_configurations.OMISSION: Omit explicit joins, replay, migration and distributed protocols when their triggering conditions are absent.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT: Remove an artefact when its consumer/risk disappears while preserving unsettled commitments.
alternative_configurations.LIMIT: A cheap representation ceases to be adequate when concurrency, turnover or delayed external actions exceed its coordination capacity.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Prescribed engine-enacted workflow
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Repeated structured work with consequential control/data/resource dependencies and a useful engine consumer.
alternative_configurations.FORM: A supported executable subset with role/work-item state, scoped handlers and recovery proportional to actual failure exposure.
alternative_configurations.SUBSTITUTION: Use block-structured constructs when they preserve required behaviour; retain general joins only for a real need.
alternative_configurations.OMISSION: No automatic need for every pattern, long-lived persistence or a model checker.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT: Simplify redundant modelling and monitoring after showing that remaining controls still protect required behaviour.
alternative_configurations.LIMIT: Control correctness alone does not validate business purpose, staffing or outside effects.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Data-centred or discretionary case support
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Legitimate next work depends on newly obtained information and skilled judgement.
alternative_configurations.FORM: Case data, eligibility and acceptance criteria delimit discretionary planning; required obligations remain distinguishable from optional activities.
alternative_configurations.SUBSTITUTION: Declarative constraints or a few prescribed subflows may protect selected invariants without fixing the whole route.
alternative_configurations.OMISSION: Do not impose one pre-enumerated path or formal acceptance cycle for every trivial act.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT: Retire planning controls with no consequential consumer; keep data and obligation references still needed.
alternative_configurations.LIMIT: Discretion requires available expertise and can make costs, consistency and progress harder to assess.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Constraint-driven or late-bound hybrid
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Stable constraints coexist with variable execution order or recurrent context-specific exceptions.
alternative_configurations.FORM: Check declarative consistency/progress and separately validate interfaces/preconditions of late-bound subprocesses.
alternative_configurations.SUBSTITUTION: A small explicit exception handler can replace an elaborate worklet repository when variability is limited.
alternative_configurations.OMISSION: No general mandate for multiple modelling languages or automated adaptation.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT: Retire obsolete rules and unused variants after accounting for live instances.
alternative_configurations.LIMIT: Constraint interaction and rule growth can destroy comprehensibility; hybrid benefits are conditional.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Long-lived cross-application coordination
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Failures, retries, version change or autonomous participants can outlive one local transaction.
alternative_configurations.FORM: Scoped message/effect contracts, sufficient persistent state, explicit uncertainty and accepted residual/transfer rules.
alternative_configurations.SUBSTITUTION: Use local atomic transactions where possible; pin old instances rather than migrate when safe and cheaper.
alternative_configurations.OMISSION: Deterministic replay is not mandatory for all durable engines; choreography does not require a central controller.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT: Retire old workers/state only after continuity and remaining external-reference obligations are satisfied.
alternative_configurations.LIMIT: Some effects cannot be queried, undone or reliably attributed; uncertainty and participant autonomy persist.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Scientific workflow execution and reproduction
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Reusable computations depend on data, code, environment and distributed resources.
alternative_configurations.FORM: Represent actual dependency/control semantics, preserve appropriate provenance and test outputs using a domain-appropriate oracle.
alternative_configurations.SUBSTITUTION: A script and environment record can be adequate for a small stable experiment; a DAG is valid for genuinely acyclic dependencies.
alternative_configurations.OMISSION: Do not import all human commitment/role mechanisms into a pure computation.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT: Remove reproducibility artefacts only when their consumers and outstanding claims no longer require them.
alternative_configurations.LIMIT: Successful execution is not scientific validity; infrastructure faults and environment drift need separate evidence.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Replay-based durable orchestration
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: The chosen engine actually uses deterministic replay of durable history.
alternative_configurations.FORM: Constrain orchestrator APIs, separate effectful activities and route histories to compatible code versions.
alternative_configurations.SUBSTITUTION: Checkpoint/state-machine recovery can realise continuity differently; side-by-side versions can avoid migration.
alternative_configurations.OMISSION: No general requirement to reconstruct every past outside state or preserve all events forever.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT: Retire version/history dependencies only after an adequate compatible checkpoint, completion or transfer.
alternative_configurations.LIMIT: Replay determinism is not semantic freshness or exactly-once arbitrary external action.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Bounded learned-component workflow — experimental
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: A learned component proposes or selects consequential actions and simpler deterministic selection is inadequate.
alternative_configurations.FORM: Keep authority, admissibility and result checks distinct from generation; inspect external semantic dependencies and uncertainty.
alternative_configurations.SUBSTITUTION: Use deterministic rules or human case decisions where they dominate on cost, accuracy or accountability.
alternative_configurations.OMISSION: Do not infer a need for agents, autonomous revision or semantic version machinery from modernity alone.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT: Remove autonomy if evaluation fails, changes are not auditable or the claimed benefit disappears.
alternative_configurations.LIMIT: General safe autonomous optimisation is UNRESOLVED; 2026 preprints are not independent deployment validation.

external_interfaces.NAME: Purpose and acceptance from organisational participants
external_interfaces.INPUT: What counts as valid work, who may accept it, obligations and contextual costs.
external_interfaces.OUTPUT: Executable or human-readable coordination constraints and qualified completion claims.
external_interfaces.BOUNDARY: Enactment cannot invent organisational purpose or legitimate authority. This is an interface to broader management, not a sibling synthesis.

external_interfaces.NAME: External applications and autonomous participants
external_interfaces.INPUT: Message/effect contracts, identifiers, delivery observations and actual outside status where available.
external_interfaces.OUTPUT: Requests, commitments, task invocations, compensation requests and explicitly qualified status.
external_interfaces.BOUNDARY: A send or local commit does not prove receipt, acceptance or effect; authority remains with the relevant participant.

external_interfaces.NAME: Human work and discretion
external_interfaces.INPUT: Task claims, context, available skill/capacity and attributable completion/acceptance declarations.
external_interfaces.OUTPUT: Offers, allocations, constraints, escalation and enough context for responsible choice.
external_interfaces.BOUNDARY: A worklist cannot certify actual performance or make absent capacity available; participation must not be replaced by log inference.

external_interfaces.NAME: Execution observations for analysis and conformance
external_interfaces.INPUT: Defined logging scope, model version and case/object correlation.
external_interfaces.OUTPUT: Qualified traces, current-state observations, anomalies and measurement limitations.
external_interfaces.BOUNDARY: Event evidence supports selected process-analysis questions. It does not answer for an unconsulted Process Mining corpus.

external_interfaces.NAME: Scientific results and semantic environments
external_interfaces.INPUT: Data, software/environment versions, acceptance oracle and relevant semantic dependencies.
external_interfaces.OUTPUT: Execution/provenance evidence and an explicitly bounded reproduction or result claim.
external_interfaces.BOUNDARY: Re-execution and deterministic history are not scientific validity or stable learned meaning.

revision_boundaries.TRIGGER: Discovered defect, changed obligation, repeated justified deviation, measured burden or environment drift.
revision_boundaries.ACTOR: The contextually authorised definition/process custodian with affected participant input; not automatically the engine or an agent.
revision_boundaries.ALLOWED_CHANGE: Propose a future definition, data/role constraint, exception policy or simpler representation.
revision_boundaries.CONTINUITY: Existing instances remain under their previous semantics until compatible coexistence or an explicitly checked state migration is selected.
revision_boundaries.EVALUATION: Relevant model checks, engine correspondence, effect/authority review and proportionate comparison; a new rule does not justify itself retroactively.

revision_boundaries.TRIGGER: A live case cannot proceed under anticipated rules.
revision_boundaries.ACTOR: The actor authorised for this exception and any separately required effect/waiver authority.
revision_boundaries.ALLOWED_CHANGE: Repair, suspend, cancel, compensate, transfer or migrate within a declared scope.
revision_boundaries.CONTINUITY: Preserve accountability for work/effects that already occurred; termination is not erasure.
revision_boundaries.EVALUATION: Current-state/data and outstanding-effect review; independent acceptance where the obligation requires it.

revision_boundaries.TRIGGER: A learned component proposes a structural optimisation or semantic dependency changes.
revision_boundaries.ACTOR: An authorised reviewer/evaluator external to the proposal’s own assertion of validity.
revision_boundaries.ALLOWED_CHANGE: Bounded proposal or experiment; no general self-authorising mutation is established.
revision_boundaries.CONTINUITY: Protect current instances and previously accepted commitments, including relevant semantic-version dependencies.
revision_boundaries.EVALUATION: Adversarial effect/authority tests and a credible benefit comparison; EWM-074 remains unresolved.

unresolved_composition_obligations.ISSUE: No single proved semantics composes all retained control/data/resource/human/external-effect mechanisms.
unresolved_composition_obligations.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: A later actual configuration must establish model/implementation and environment correspondence; do not combine theorems with incompatible assumptions.

unresolved_composition_obligations.ISSUE: External action may remain unobservable or irreversible.
unresolved_composition_obligations.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: A declared acceptance, residual or transfer rule with legitimate authority; uncertainty cannot be logged away.

unresolved_composition_obligations.ISSUE: General safe autonomous workflow optimisation is not established.
unresolved_composition_obligations.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Independent prospective comparisons, adversarial semantic/authority/effect checks and evidence of stable benefit.

unresolved_composition_obligations.ISSUE: Comparative benefit and participant burden of hybrid flexibility are not generally quantified.
unresolved_composition_obligations.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Real variation, user understanding, exception cost and an adequate cheaper baseline.

unresolved_composition_obligations.ISSUE: A complete technical adjudication of the original Börger critique is limited by access.
unresolved_composition_obligations.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Lawful full original text and analysis of its exact technical claims; no settlement inferred from the response.

domain_models.NAME: Definition / instance / work-item semantics
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: A definition D_v supplies activities, constraints and a declared semantics at version v. An instance I=(case,v,control,data,work,interaction,recovery references) is one enactment, not D_v itself. An event e may induce I -> I_prime under D_v. A work item is an offered or undertaken unit within I; an external business object X has its own identity and state. This tuple is an analytical interface, not the exact storage schema of WfMC or any engine. Enabled(I,a), Authorised(actor,a), Able(actor,a) and EffectAchieved(X,a) are different predicates. Their distinctions may be implicit in a tiny manual procedure, but must not be conflated when consequences depend on them.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: Definition version, case, work item, attempt and external object need distinct equality/lifetime meanings where they can diverge; separate databases or UUIDs are not mandatory.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: An enabling rule determines permitted transitions, not necessarily one predetermined next task; multiple actions and recurring interaction can remain enabled.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Inputs and incoming events must be bound to the right scope and case; an identifier alone does not validate its referent or value.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: An enactment model can offer work but cannot create availability, competence or external authority; a single known performer is a valid simple case.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: Correctness first names the predicate and model. A correct transition or terminal state is not automatically a valid business result.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: The definition must say which work is stopped or continued by an exception; a non-engine procedure may use an explicit human decision instead.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: An external action changes X through the responsible participant. The model records a claim/observation; compensation, when available, is a further action.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: Persist only facts/references needed for the chosen continuity claim. When recovery is irrelevant for an ephemeral action, no durable engine is implied.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: An instance must retain an intelligible governing definition; changing D_v does not automatically migrate I or revise past outside actions.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: The model observes its declared interface; request, declaration, acceptance and result can be different observations.

domain_models.LIMITS: No universal state model or compulsory engine architecture is claimed. Purpose and acceptable consequence remain supplied by the actual context.

domain_models.NAME: Control-flow coordination
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: Let A be the semantic activation scope for a split, loop entry or subworkflow call. Branch membership B_A and a join predicate J_A(current marking, possible future arrivals) determine convergence. For a fixed AND-join, all required inputs must be present; for inclusive joins, whether another input can still arrive can be non-local. Cancellation changes the state on which J_A is evaluated but is not generally a success arrival. Multiple-instance thresholds, race arbitration and termination use separate predicates. A may be represented by net state rather than an explicit tagged identifier. Recursion has a parent-child continuation relation; an available base case alone does not force it to be selected.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: Correlate branch arrivals to the intended case and activation. Recursion introduces distinct invocation instances, whether represented explicitly or by the formal semantics.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: Sequence, choice, splits, synchronisation, merging, multiple instances, deferred choice, interleaving, loops and cancellation are alternative constructs with different enabling rules.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Guards need defined input and missing-value semantics; binding and concurrent update assumptions cannot be inferred from graph edges.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: Token readiness does not establish worker/resource readiness; critical sections only exclude actors in their enforced scope.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: Pattern satisfaction is a local/contextual behavioural claim. General joins may need non-local analysis and do not inherit every ordinary-net composition theorem.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: Specify cancelled region, interrupted activity and downstream join effects; termination may be local while external work continues.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: Control cancellation and merging do not undo outside effects; successful control convergence can coexist with unsuccessful task consequences.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: Recovery must not double-count arrivals or mix activation scopes. Pure in-memory calculations may instead be safely recomputed.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: Changing a join or loop while a case runs requires compatibility with its current arrivals and active work, not only a valid new graph.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: A displayed token or branch status reflects model state; hidden worker activity and delayed events may differ.

domain_models.LIMITS: Block structure, unrestricted graphs and DAGs are selected by required behaviours and analysis cost; no universal preference is imposed.

domain_models.NAME: Soundness and model limits
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: For an ordinary WF-net N=(P,T,F) with source i and sink o and each node on an i-to-o path, start with marking [i]. Classical soundness requires: (1) for every reachable M, there exists a firing sequence to [o]; (2) if a reachable M contains an o token, then M=[o]; (3) every transition can occur in some execution from [i]. This does not say every run eventually finishes. The short-circuited-net characterisation connects soundness to liveness/boundedness under the stated ordinary-net model. Other soundness variants change populations or quantifiers. Reset arcs, data, time and resource extensions change what can be proved and how. Model-to-engine correspondence is a separate argument.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: The theorem’s population and initial marking are part of the claim; one case does not automatically establish a many-case property.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: Transition firing follows the selected net semantics. A possible completing continuation is not an observed scheduling policy or inevitable progress.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Ordinary control-flow abstractions omit data values unless explicitly extended; false or missing business inputs remain outside the proof.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: Unconstrained transitions abstract human availability and authority. Resource/time feasibility needs a separate model or operational evidence.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: The guarantee is the exact soundness variant for the exact net class. Reduction and composition must preserve that property; general reset-net undecidability does not forbid all bounded analysis.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: Cancellation needs an appropriate extended model or bounded analysis; adding it can invalidate a proof over the original ordinary net.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: Final marking is not proof of material success, accurate output or a successfully executed compensation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: A structural theorem does not by itself specify crash persistence or external retry handling. Add those only when the claimed scope includes them.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: A theorem about a new definition is not a proof that a current marking/data state can migrate into it.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: A model-checker result proves an abstract property if its encoding is faithful, not unmodelled organisational facts.

domain_models.LIMITS: Formal validity is often strong while comparative deployment benefit is weak or absent. No theorem is refuted merely by an implementation violating its assumptions.

domain_models.NAME: Data and correlation
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: An input binding names a producer/value, scope and binding time. A guard can evaluate true, false, unresolved or error according to the selected semantics; missing values are not silently assigned a universal interpretation. Correlation maps an incoming message to zero, one or more candidate cases; ambiguous/no-match outcomes require an explicit rule. Business-object identity is distinct from case, work item and message identity. Data-centric models use lifecycle state and available information to permit work. Concurrent mutation adds a snapshot/conflict/isolation choice that must fit the decision being made.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: Case, document/object, task and message identities have separate lifecycles; interacting objects need not fit one artificial one-to-one case key.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: Data availability and value predicates can enable or constrain work independently of control tokens; data-dependent errors require more than syntactic graph validity.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Declare scope, copy/reference/shared semantics, ownership, binding time, correlation rule and freshness required for each consequential input.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: Data access policy and action authority require a basis beyond case membership; a visible input is not necessarily permitted for every use.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: Availability, type and correlation correctness do not establish truth of the underlying data or every business invariant.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: Skips, cancellation and repairs can remove a producer or change the input expected by a later task; check those paths.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: An external source may commit a change while the workflow holds stale data; neither copying nor logging restores the original world.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: Retries need stable operation keys and a policy for re-reading or preserving inputs; both blind reuse and blind refresh can be wrong.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: Migration must preserve required input history and pending correlation meanings or deliberately transform them with a justified rule.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: The engine sees the values supplied to it, not automatically the current or correct state of external business objects.

domain_models.LIMITS: This packet does not prescribe a universal isolation level, global shared store, access policy or legal permission model.

domain_models.NAME: Resources and human work
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: The work-item lifecycle distinguishes the needed states among enabled/offered, allocated, started, suspended, resumed, completed, failed and withdrawn. These are a vocabulary, not a mandatory universal sequence. An authorisation relation U x T and cross-task constraints define permissible assignments; satisfying them does not solve time ordering or provide available workers. Delegation transfers a declared state and responsibility only under applicable constraints. A person’s declaration and a recipient’s acceptance are evidence-bearing interactions, distinct from the material result.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: Work item and performer identity must survive handover; the person occupying a role can change during a long case.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: Enabling, offering, claiming and starting have different consumers and need only be separated where their distinction changes coordination.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Provide the performer with necessary data and handover context; prior external actions must not vanish during reassignment.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: Role eligibility, permission, competence, calendar availability and capacity are different assumptions; duty constraints may make an assignment globally infeasible.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: Workflow satisfiability addresses assignment under a specific constraint language; the inspected WSP model explicitly does not solve time ordering.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: Withdrawal, suspension and delegation require treatment of still-running work; a reassignment label does not physically stop the old performer.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: A human click or report is evidence of a declaration, not automatic verification of the intended external effect. Risk may justify trusting that declaration.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: Recovery must identify the current responsible party and any abandoned or continuing work; a simple acknowledged handover may suffice.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: Changes to roles, rules or task meaning can invalidate an assignment mid-case and need a relevant recheck, not necessarily universal migration.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: Informal coordination and work outside the system may be material. More instrumentation can be intrusive and still incomplete.

domain_models.LIMITS: No compulsory surveillance, independence-of-witness rule or new authority is inferred. Fairness and workload goals require actual participants and context.

domain_models.NAME: Exceptions, cancellation and compensation
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: An exception response is analysed along work-item, case and recovery dimensions. Interrupting stops or requests stopping the affected scope; non-interrupting creates additional handling while original work may continue. Requested, acknowledged and observed cessation may differ. A timeout establishes missing expected response/progress. If action f has changed external state X, compensation c is a further relation from the then-current state, not generally f inverse. Residual obligations may be fulfilled, legitimately waived, transferred or explicitly accepted as unresolved; this classification is an analytical closure interface, not a vendor lifecycle.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: Identify the affected item, containing scope, action attempt and external operation before cancellation or repair.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: Define what remains enabled after handler activation; cancellation is not universally a success input to a later join.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Handlers need current context and prior-effect identity; incomplete detection/classification is itself a limit.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: The handler or operator needs authority for each remedy, which may differ from the authority for the original action.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: Correct handler control-flow does not prove complete exception detection, successful stopping or restored business state.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: Interrupt, cancellation, termination and suspension differ; specify propagation and independently continuing work.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: Compensation is a fallible forward action with restricted scope. Irreversible effects and new intervening facts can prevent exact restoration.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: Timeouts and lost responses require safe retry or reconciliation; failed remedies cannot be silently treated as completed.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: A repair can be case-specific; changing a handler for future instances does not retroactively repair an already interrupted state.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: An engine may record cancellation before a worker stops; external success/failure can remain unknown.

domain_models.LIMITS: No universal rollback or infallible compensator exists. Closure may be legitimate with accepted residual work, but cannot misstate it as fulfilled.

domain_models.NAME: Interorganisational interaction and commitment
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: Participants P_i control local transition systems. A shared protocol constrains observable messages and commitments without necessarily exposing private states or installing a central controller. Sent, received, accepted, declared performed and accepted-as-satisfactory distinguish information transport from operative commitments; only distinctions needed by the relationship must be materialised. Local soundness plus channel composition can fail globally when participants’ waits or order assumptions disagree. The inspected formal model assumes predefined asynchronous partners and abstracts resources/data, whereas actual participant autonomy requires additional evidence.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: Message, partner, business object and case identity must be matched across organisational boundaries; local IDs may require mappings.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: Local orchestration and shared protocol/choreography constrain different transition systems; global compatibility is not automatic from local validity.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Message contracts specify fields, correlation, ordering and error interpretation; schema validity alone does not establish shared meaning.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: Each participant retains its effective authority and capacity. An agreed protocol cannot make an unwilling or unavailable participant act.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: Compatibility/completion claims are bounded by partner and channel models. Open strategic participants are not validated by a closed cooperative proof.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: One party’s timeout or cancellation request may not stop another party’s work; negotiate continuation and rejection semantics.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: External action belongs to its performer; compensation or waiver may require new agreement from affected participants.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: Lost/duplicate/reordered messages and externally committed actions need an explicitly chosen retry/reconciliation protocol.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: Protocol and definition versions can coexist only if pending messages and commitments remain interpretable.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: Central monitoring sees exchanged signals, not every partner’s private state or actual satisfaction.

domain_models.LIMITS: The language-action cycle is useful for some cooperative work, not an exhaustive ontology or automatic proof of informed consent.

domain_models.NAME: Persistence, replay and recovery
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: Let H be persisted coordination evidence, I its reconstructed state and X the external state that may differ. Recovery must justify the next action from H plus any necessary observation of X. Replay-based runtimes constrain the command sequence produced from recorded history; nondeterministic I/O is isolated/recorded through the runtime contract. Other workflow implementations use different persistence mechanisms and need not obey the same programming rule. Exactly-once output claims require a declared cooperative boundary: ExoFlow explicitly depends on determinism classification and idempotency or idempotent rollback, among other persistence conditions.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: Retain case, version, work-item, attempt and intended business-operation identity at the granularity needed for recovery.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: Recovery restores a justified enabled set rather than blindly restarting the last visible activity; command replay is a specific implementation discipline.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Know which inputs are frozen and which must be re-read; preserve correlation and deduplication keys for the relevant horizon.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: Work-item ownership after crash must be resolved; technical replay cannot make an unavailable person or service act.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: Durable/replay correctness and business-effect count are separate claims. A scoped exactly-once theorem is not a universal effect guarantee.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: Cancellation may be cooperative and delayed; recovery must consider live workers and remedies, not only terminal engine status.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: An outside action may have committed without a recorded acknowledgement. Idempotency, transactions or reconciliation must cover that boundary.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: Choose sufficient checkpoint/history/intent evidence and test crash points. Retention is based on consumers and obligations, not forever by default.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: Compatible code and governing definitions must remain identifiable. Pinning, coexistence or checked migration are alternative continuity strategies.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: Persisted history is authoritative about recorded decisions only under its integrity assumptions, not automatically about current external reality.

domain_models.LIMITS: No exact storage design, fixed retention time or universal replay engine is prescribed. External uncertainty may force bounded manual adjudication.

domain_models.NAME: Dynamic change and flexible/case execution
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: A migration is a guarded relation mu from an instance governed by D_v to an instance governed by D_w. The guard examines current control/data state, completed/pending work and relevant interaction obligations. Sound(D_w) alone does not imply mu is valid. Flexibility by design selects an anticipated branch; deviation permits bounded departure; underspecification leaves parts to later choice; change revises the governing definition/state. Declarative rules constrain allowed finite traces and pending obligations. Case handling makes available data and actor judgement central. Worklets late-bind a subworkflow using contextual rules. These remain alternative or combined configurations, not one compulsory ladder.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: Keep the current case and its historical/version context intelligible across change; new cases may simply start under a new definition.
