DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: Prescribed paths, allowed-trace constraints and discretionary plan items have different enabling/completion rules that require explicit coupling.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Changes must preserve or deliberately remap required inputs, past data and pending message bindings.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: Authorised planners and reviewers determine which changes or discretionary actions are permitted; technical edit capability is insufficient.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: Check current-state migration validity, rule consistency and relevant progress assumptions. A sound target or individually sensible constraints are insufficient.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: An exception can justify case repair without becoming a general rule; new definitions do not automatically resolve existing exceptions.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: Past outside actions remain facts to reconcile, even if the model is revised; state edit or model undo is not physical compensation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: Recovery and version continuity must still work after change; pinning or coexistence may be cheaper than automatic migration.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: Declare change population, compatible state mapping, deployment selection and retirement conditions for old definitions.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: History of formal changes may omit informal adaptations; participant feedback is needed where that affects continuation or interpretation.

domain_models.LIMITS: Greater freedom is not always better. Choose by uncertainty, skill, required constraints and verification/communication cost.

domain_models.NAME: Monitoring and external correspondence
domain_models.STATE_AND_RELATIONS: An observation function O maps some aspects of an actual execution/world history into recorded events. O is generally not injective: two worlds can produce the same completion click while differing in whether work occurred. Conformance evaluates a model against that chosen log abstraction, not every fact about the world. Monitoring needs a consumer who can distinguish explanations and take an authorised action. Scientific rerun success and output validity are separate; static low-code/agent definitions and observed runtime performance are separate evidence objects. Semantic-environment compatibility is a current proposal whose adequacy needs evaluation.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.DEFINITION_INSTANCE_AND_WORK_ITEM_IDENTI: Logs require declared case/work-item/attempt/object mapping; a single-case projection may omit many-object relationships.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CONTROL_FLOW_AND_ENABLING_SEMANTICS: Observed ordering must fit the model’s semantics; timestamps or display order do not automatically establish causality.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.DATA_AND_CORRELATION_ASSUMPTIONS: Events may omit payload, provenance, freshness or downstream acknowledgement needed for a stronger claim.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.RESOURCE_AVAILABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY: Human work outside the engine may be material; monitoring creates no automatic authority to intervene or surveil.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.SOUNDNESS_OR_CORRECTNESS_MODEL: Conformance, test execution and performance metrics support distinct questions. Neither fitness nor a successful exit validates the business/scientific result.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXCEPTION_INTERRUPT_AND_CANCELLATION_SCO: Error and cancellation records describe detected/reported events; undetected failures and overlapping fault categories limit diagnosis.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_AND_COMPENSATION_BOUNDAR: An event-to-world claim needs an appropriate observation or acceptance source; repeated copies of one record are not independent corroboration.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PERSISTENCE_RETRY_AND_RECOVERY_OBLIGATIO: Keep the evidence needed for actual recovery/review consumers and know what compaction removes; complete logging is not a universal obligation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.VERSION_AND_RUNNING_INSTANCE_MIGRATION: Definition, engine, data and semantic-environment versions affect interpretation; static template exports may hide code and configuration.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.ENGINE_OR_MODEL_OBSERVABILITY_LIMIT: Every monitored claim is bounded by the recorder’s observation and the study’s sampling. Current preprints/static corpora do not establish general causal benefit.

domain_models.LIMITS: The formal observation-function account is this report’s explanatory abstraction, not a new empirical result. Its purpose is to prevent stronger claims than the evidence allows.

nodes.NAME: Office information systems, document routing and heterogeneous precursors
nodes.PROBLEM: Coordinate office information, documents, tasks and applications rather than only individual computations.
nodes.MECHANISM: Plural office/document, image, database, messaging and transaction technologies later converge in workflow enactment.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: The reference model gives an explicit heterogeneous ancestry, not one engine as the inventor of the field.
nodes.LIMITS: Ellis and Nutt 1980 was verified bibliographically only; detailed original mechanisms are not reconstructed from unread text.
nodes.RECEPTION: WfMC’s later taxonomy documents a retrospective convergence; it does not settle the earliest invention or every influence edge.

nodes.NAME: Situated and cooperative-work criticism
nodes.PROBLEM: Formal routes may omit the practical work through which people interpret plans and coordinate.
nodes.MECHANISM: Freeflow mediates representation/action; activity-theoretic design treats plans as resources used in situated work.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Criticism changes the default from rigid enforcement to conditional support and participant involvement.
nodes.LIMITS: Suchman 1983 and Bowers et al. 1995 originals are access-limited; direct evidence comes from inspected later work, not an invented reconstruction.
nodes.RECEPTION: Freeflow and Bardram explicitly engage the criticism; neither establishes that all formal models are harmful.

nodes.NAME: Long-lived transactions and Sagas
nodes.PROBLEM: Long-running work cannot always retain one atomic database transaction and its locks.
nodes.MECHANISM: Decompose work into committed components with compensating and forward-recovery actions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Separates practical long-lived recovery from ordinary atomic rollback.
nodes.LIMITS: Compensation is fallible and constrained by available inverse/remedial actions; physical equivalence is not guaranteed.
nodes.RECEPTION: Later workflow exception/recovery accounts import this distinction, while specific engines implement different boundaries.

nodes.NAME: ActionWorkflow and the language-action branch
nodes.PROBLEM: Coordination requires commitments and acceptance, not only transmission of information or material steps.
nodes.MECHANISM: Distinguish proposal, agreement, performance declaration and satisfaction within an interaction.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Adds an explicit relational consumer to completion and supports incremental automation.
nodes.LIMITS: Developer-origin account; its speech-act structure need not describe every kind of work or consent.
nodes.RECEPTION: A native alternative account of workflow purpose; retained selectively rather than made a compulsory four-step ritual.

nodes.NAME: WfMC Workflow Reference Model
nodes.PROBLEM: Heterogeneous workflow systems need shared terms, interfaces and separation of definition from enactment.
nodes.MECHANISM: Reference objects and interfaces connect build-time definitions, run-time services, worklists, applications and administration.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Consolidates architecture and vocabulary without requiring a particular engine internals.
nodes.LIMITS: Interface standardisation does not prove runtime semantic equivalence, adoption or economic benefit.
nodes.RECEPTION: The 2004 retrospective criticises continuing information-marshalling and integration limits.

nodes.NAME: Workflow nets, Woflan and soundness variants
nodes.PROBLEM: Syntactically plausible models can deadlock, leave residual work or contain dead tasks.
nodes.MECHANISM: Petri-net analysis, short-circuit reasoning and reductions; later classification of distinct soundness predicates and decidability boundaries.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Makes completion claims precise and separates stronger/weaker models rather than using correctness as one undifferentiated label.
nodes.LIMITS: Formal assumptions and implementation correspondence are mandatory; reset/cancellation extensions change analysis possibilities.
nodes.RECEPTION: Later YAWL and declarative work reuse and extend verification concerns without inheriting every theorem.

nodes.DATE: Programme origins described retrospectively as 1999; article 2003; revised report 2006
nodes.NAME: Workflow control-flow patterns
nodes.PROBLEM: Products and languages use similar words for materially different coordination behaviour.
nodes.MECHANISM: Pattern vocabulary and increasingly explicit contextual semantics distinguish choices, joins, concurrency, repetition and termination.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Original twenty and twenty-three additions in the revised report yield 43 control-flow patterns, not a requirement to install them all.
nodes.LIMITS: Context assumptions, completeness and evaluation claims are disputed; pattern support is not a full product-quality measure.
nodes.RECEPTION: YAWL explicitly responds to expressive gaps; the 2012 dispute remains partly access-limited.

nodes.DATE: 2004 data report; 2005 resource paper; 2006 exception paper
nodes.NAME: Data, resource and exception perspectives
nodes.PROBLEM: Control-flow alone cannot capture information availability, human work allocation or recovery behaviour.
nodes.MECHANISM: Separate but coupled taxonomies of data scope/binding, work-item lifecycle/resource rules, and exception detection/handling.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Exposes additional enactment obligations rather than treating token flow as a complete organisational model.
nodes.LIMITS: Taxonomies and historical tool comparisons are not deployment frequencies; exception analysis may assume prompt detection/classification.
nodes.RECEPTION: The multi-perspective view informs later process-aware systems and this synthesis’s joint-readiness model.

nodes.DATE: 2005 journal article, earlier technical work acknowledged
nodes.NAME: YAWL
nodes.PROBLEM: Existing workflow languages inadequately express selected patterns and cancellation/join semantics.
nodes.MECHANISM: A formal workflow language combines Petri-net ancestry with multiple instances, cancellation regions and OR-joins.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: An explicit extension directed by pattern-derived requirements.
nodes.LIMITS: Important composition results exclude unrestricted OR-join cases; expressiveness brings verification cost.
nodes.RECEPTION: Used as a base for worklets and related research, not evidence that one engine unifies the whole field.

nodes.NAME: ADEPTflex and adaptive running-instance change
nodes.PROBLEM: Unexpected change must not destroy the validity of already running cases.
nodes.MECHANISM: Admissible graph/schema operations are coupled to state and data transformations with preconditions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Running-instance validity becomes a separate burden from target-definition correctness.
nodes.LIMITS: Model and supported-operation bounds; prototype-era evidence, not arbitrary migration correctness.
nodes.RECEPTION: Later flexibility classifications preserve change as one mode among alternatives rather than a universal cure.

nodes.NAME: Inter-organisational workflows
nodes.PROBLEM: Local process correctness does not ensure compatible exchange between autonomous participants.
nodes.MECHANISM: Loosely coupled local workflow models plus explicit communication places/contracts support composition analysis.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Separates a participant’s local view from global interaction conditions.
nodes.LIMITS: The analysed communication/reliability model bounds results; organisational agreement cannot be manufactured by a net.
nodes.RECEPTION: Executable orchestration and choreography address related interfaces; a direct influence on each standard is not assumed.

nodes.NAME: Business artifacts and data-centric operational specification
nodes.PROBLEM: Activity-centric descriptions can obscure the business objects whose evolving data define useful work.
nodes.MECHANISM: Represent business artifacts, their relevant data and operational lifecycle.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Provides a data-centred unit of analysis and coordination alternative.
nodes.LIMITS: Interacting artifacts still require correlation, access and global consistency obligations.
nodes.RECEPTION: Shares concerns with case handling, but similarity alone is not documentary proof of derivation.

nodes.NAME: Case handling
nodes.PROBLEM: Knowledge-intensive cases require discretion and relevant information beyond one activity worklist.
nodes.MECHANISM: Make the case and its data central, allowing authorised performers to choose available work.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: A principled alternative to purely activity-centred routing.
nodes.LIMITS: Information access does not create skill or legitimate authority; universal performance superiority is not shown.
nodes.RECEPTION: Related case-management standardisation later exposes discretionary planning; strict historical derivation is not claimed.

nodes.NAME: Worklets
nodes.PROBLEM: Repeated contextual exceptions require controlled flexibility without redesigning the whole workflow every time.
nodes.MECHANISM: Select small context-sensitive subprocesses through a rule-based worklet service.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Hybridises a workflow engine with contextual selection and incremental exception reuse.
nodes.LIMITS: Rule proliferation, interface incompatibility and context drift remain possible.
nodes.RECEPTION: Explicit YAWL implementation and documented use of ripple-down-rule ideas; not autonomous unconstrained self-revision.

nodes.NAME: Declarative constraint-based workflows
nodes.PROBLEM: A complete prescribed order can be needlessly restrictive where only selected constraints matter.
nodes.MECHANISM: Describe allowed behaviour using constraints and verify their interactions through formal representations.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Changes freedom from choosing one path to choosing among constraint-admissible behaviours.
nodes.LIMITS: Consistency, dead activities, pending obligations and intelligibility remain real burdens.
nodes.RECEPTION: The 2008 flexibility taxonomy places declarative methods among alternatives, not at the inevitable end of a progress line.

nodes.DATE: 2007 BPEL 2.0; inspected BPMN edition 2014; CMMN edition 2016
nodes.NAME: Executable service and process/case standards
nodes.PROBLEM: Shared interchange and execution notation must support service interaction, events, tasks and discretionary cases.
nodes.MECHANISM: BPEL specifies orchestration/correlation; BPMN combines model and executable constructs; CMMN specifies case planning/lifecycles.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Standardised obligations and vocabulary can improve explicitness without making all three notations equivalent.
nodes.LIMITS: Conformance classes, extensions, underspecification and implementations limit portability; these edition dates are not field-origin dates.
nodes.RECEPTION: Historical engine tests show incomplete support and regressions; exact current version claims are limited to inspected pages.

nodes.DATE: 1998 audit specification; 2008 conformance work; field study published 2016
nodes.NAME: Execution observations and practical evaluation
nodes.PROBLEM: Enactment needs meaningful histories, and practical benefit cannot be inferred from a design diagram.
nodes.MECHANISM: Audit event semantics, model/log comparison and contextual longitudinal observation.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Connects execution records to explicit analytic consumers and supplies negative/attrition evidence about deployment.
nodes.LIMITS: Records omit outside work; conformance and adoption do not establish causal benefit.
nodes.RECEPTION: This is a documented intersection with process analysis/mining; no sibling Evolved output is used.

nodes.DATE: 2013 inspected Taverna edition; 2023 Yevis; 2025 PanDA study presentation
nodes.NAME: Scientific workflow translation
nodes.PROBLEM: Scientific work coordinates computations, services, data and environments across reuse and failure.
nodes.MECHANISM: Workflow engines combine iteration/dependency control, provenance, execution validation and distributed resource management.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Translates coordination into computational and reproducibility settings with different acceptance oracles.
nodes.LIMITS: Service/environment decay and successful-but-wrong outputs limit reproduction claims; accessed failure-study originals vary in depth.
nodes.RECEPTION: The inspected Taverna version has loops/streaming; scientific workflow is not uniformly DAG-only.

nodes.DATE: 2023 ExoFlow; 2024 DSE version; live docs inspected 2026
nodes.NAME: Durable execution and cloud orchestration
nodes.PROBLEM: Crashes, retries and long histories must not lose or duplicate consequential work.
nodes.MECHANISM: Persistent state/checkpoints, replay or speculative recovery operate under declared determinism and effect assumptions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Makes recovery semantics a first-class execution concern while reusing long-lived coordination questions.
nodes.LIMITS: Scoped exactly-once results do not encompass arbitrary external effects; replay and version compatibility are implementation-specific.
nodes.RECEPTION: A translation/convergence with prior workflow concerns, not proof that modern branding invented durability.

nodes.NAME: Low-code, agent/workflow hybrids and semantic-environment proposals
nodes.PROBLEM: Visual and learned orchestration can hide runtime actions and depend on changing semantic context.
nodes.MECHANISM: Static template analysis and proposed semantic-isolation contracts separate design wiring, runtime effects and compatibility assumptions. The semantic-isolation prototype also compares controlled anomaly prevention and a late-discovery case.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Raises testable questions about authority, validation and semantic drift in durable learned workflows.
nodes.LIMITS: New preprints, selected static corpora and no independent broad safety/effectiveness demonstration.
nodes.RECEPTION: Kept as assumption-sensitive frontier mechanisms and an unresolved autonomous-optimisation claim, not mature consensus.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: The WfMC account explicitly describes heterogeneous document/office/application precursors.
edges.LIMIT: A retrospective account does not establish every earliest inventor.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Situated-work criticism challenges route-centred enactment; inspected Freeflow explicitly positions its mediation alternative against strict execution.
edges.LIMIT: This is a critique of a family of systems, not evidence that WfMC adopted Freeflow.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Woflan contrasts semantic validation with syntax-oriented exchange and supplies a bounded formal analysis.
edges.LIMIT: Formal correctness does not repair organisational mismatch by itself.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: YAWL explicitly extends Petri-net-oriented workflow modelling with selected pattern mechanisms.
edges.LIMIT: Additional constructs do not automatically retain all ordinary-net theorems.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: YAWL is explicitly motivated by expressiveness identified through workflow patterns.
edges.LIMIT: This does not show independently superior deployment outcomes.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Pattern investigations extend beyond control flow into data, resource and exception perspectives.
edges.LIMIT: Distinct perspectives are not a single fully compositional semantics by default.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Revised patterns separate previously conflated assumptions; the later critique/response disputes evaluation and specification claims.
edges.LIMIT: The original critique is only abstract-accessible; its technical dispute is not marked resolved.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Workflow exception treatment explicitly uses compensation as distinct from ordinary rollback.
edges.LIMIT: Every handler is not a saga, and compensation may be unavailable.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Case handling and cooperative-work criticism both oppose rigid activity-only routing.
edges.LIMIT: No unsupported one-way intellectual derivation is asserted.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Both make business objects/case data central rather than treating data as incidental to a route.
edges.LIMIT: Convergence is not exact semantic equivalence or proven influence.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: The worklet service is implemented as an extension in the YAWL setting.
edges.LIMIT: Interface and selection preconditions still require checking.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Both address changing circumstances, with state transformation versus late-bound selection.
edges.LIMIT: Their mechanisms differ; one is not simply a renamed version of the other.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Declarative work employs formal behavioural verification to detect conflicts/dead activities.
edges.LIMIT: Finite/trace constraints and ordinary workflow-net predicates are not interchangeable.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Both seek flexibility, but one changes existing process structure/state and the other permits multiple constraint-compliant paths.
edges.LIMIT: Selection depends on where uncertainty lies; no universal replacement is shown.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: The inspected BPMN specification includes explicit pattern mappings in its execution discussion.
edges.LIMIT: Citation/mapping documents engagement, not exclusive derivation of BPMN.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Inter-organisational workflow and executable service orchestration share process/message coordination questions.
edges.LIMIT: A direct influence on every standard is not established.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Case handling and CMMN both address case-level data and discretion.
edges.LIMIT: The case-management field is broader than the single case-handling paper.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: WfMC audit data specifies records produced by enactment services within the reference-model family.
edges.LIMIT: This is a record interface, not a modern universal retention obligation.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Conformance checking relates formal process behaviour to recorded observations.
edges.LIMIT: Observation completeness and business meaning remain separate.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: The longitudinal study examines whether the promised organisational benefit actually materialises, including abandonment.
edges.LIMIT: The evidence comes from distinct programmes; no experimental lineage is invented.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Scientific engines use workflow definitions, execution and application/service coordination for computational research.
edges.LIMIT: This is a field translation, not proof of one documented WfMC-to-Taverna dependency.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Long-lived and durable execution share the problem of recovery around effects that outlast a local transaction.
edges.LIMIT: Modern recovery protocols are not assumed to descend only from Sagas.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: DAG execution combines workflow dependencies with fault-tolerant distributed computing and checkpoint/effect controls.
edges.LIMIT: The scientific/DAG boundary is explicit and does not erase other workflow forms.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: The semantic-isolation proposal explicitly extends the concern from durable execution to changing semantic environments.
edges.LIMIT: A proposed extension is not established or independently validated practice.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Low-code template study analyses visual execution and configuration relationships in an agent-enabled workflow ecosystem.
edges.LIMIT: A product corpus is not representative evidence for every workflow language.

edges.RELATION_BASIS: Both use agent terminology but the 1992 agent processor and contemporary LLM components are different mechanisms.
edges.LIMIT: No LLM ancestry or equivalence is inferred from vocabulary.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Formal procedure can conceal the situated coordination, negotiation and judgement needed to get real work done.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Freeflow and Bardram supply inspected design/workplace arguments; the original Suchman and Bowers texts remain access-limited. Bardram’s ward study is qualitative, not an outcome experiment.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Preserve plans as resources for accountable action, participant feedback and bounded discretion; do not infer that every procedure is oppressive or useless.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Rigid universal prescription is narrowed. Case handling and language-action interaction remain conditional alternatives; no all-purpose ontology of work is accepted.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: The comparative costs and distribution of discretion need setting-specific evidence. Unread foundational methods are not reconstructed.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Successful deployments are a selected subset, and improvements do not establish universal causal benefit from workflow automation.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The longitudinal programme began with ten organisations/25 processes; five organisations enacted seven processes, with five validated simulation comparisons. Failures and exclusions are material, not discarded as non-workflow. Successful implementations often improved performance; abandoned programmes were primarily affected by management/ownership change or overspending, not established technical engine failures.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Include attrition, baseline and costs, and separate observed before/after changes from calibrated simulation and causal attribution. Preserve the positive adjusted comparisons while keeping their exceptions and avoid attributing organisational cancellation to a technical defect.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: EWM-071 is not retained; EWM-063 is contextual rather than a general return-on-investment claim.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: No randomised or broadly representative benefit estimate is established; outcomes cannot be pooled across unrelated settings.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Pattern lists and notations may lack sufficient precision or faithfulness; popularity is not a technical rebuttal.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Börger’s abstract and full rejoinder were inspected, but the full detailed critique was unavailable. The authors’ response clarifies intended use and rejects a universal feature mandate.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Use explicit operational semantics and context assumptions, while leaving unread technical disputes unresolved rather than awarding either side a blanket victory.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: The taxonomy remains useful but is not accepted as a complete behavioural semantics or compulsory maximal feature set.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Specific formal counterarguments in the inaccessible article were not adjudicated in detail.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A single join or termination label conflates different branch, loop, multiplicity and cancellation assumptions.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The 2006 revised view explicitly splits structured, acyclic and general synchronising merges and adds region/multiple-instance cancellation; YAWL’s general joins have non-local implications.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Choose the narrowest adequate semantics, and test cancelled/late/re-entered branches for the actual model.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Universal DAG restriction and all-patterns maximalism are rejected; expressive constructs remain conditional.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Complex joins and cancellation can impose expensive non-local reasoning.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A sound control model does not establish resources, deadlines, fairness or successful external action.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The inspected soundness definitions quantify over reachable markings; the WSP formulation separately abstracts time ordering.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Keep structural, assignment, progress and outcome arguments distinct and couple only those relevant to the claim.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: EWM-015/016/029/040 remain assumption-sensitive; EWM-019 explicitly adds a separate feasibility burden.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: It is context-specific which omitted environmental assumptions can be validated.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Adding cancellation/reset behaviour can change decidability and invalidate simple compositional arguments.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Reset-arc soundness results and YAWL theorem restrictions were inspected; no result is extended to every finite implementation.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Use a suitable bounded model, restriction, abstraction or partial analysis with stated limits rather than assert automatic global verification.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Formal verification remains conditional; neither universal tractability nor universal impossibility is accepted.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Practical abstraction fidelity and scaling remain implementation-specific.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A valid control diagram can route missing, stale or wrongly correlated data; some standard binding details are intentionally underspecified.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: BPMN multiple-instance data discussion and BPEL correlation were read. ADEPT makes state/data conditions relevant to change. The Maude 2023 lead is metadata-only and contributes no proof.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Identify bindings, correlation, freshness and missing-input semantics at the real decision point.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Data/control integration is retained without claiming to verify all value semantics or impose one isolation level.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Advanced data-verification results in inaccessible recent work are not adjudicated.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Role assignment is not available, competent, authorised human capacity; feasible individual assignments can be globally inconsistent.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Resource patterns and WSP address different parts of allocation. The qualitative hospital work shows why actual practice matters, without measuring a universal scheduling effect.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Keep eligibility, authority, availability and duty constraints separate; supply only needed lifecycle distinctions and escalation.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Satisfiability and feasibility are not conflated. Fairness/priority optimisation remains conditional.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Incentives and actual authority depend on the organisation and cannot be inferred from a model.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Declaration, terminal state and recipient satisfaction can diverge from the material result.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: ActionWorkflow distinguishes communication commitments; CMMN completion permits specified terminal states that are not success; Yevis states its execution tests do not check expected output.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Specify the exact completion/result claim and proportionate evidence; allow trustworthy human declarations where sufficient.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: EWM-030/058 retain the distinction. Mandatory independent witnessing and universal log truth are not accepted.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Acceptance may be uninformed or coerced; observation may be expensive or unavailable.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Timeout or cancellation status is not proof that external work failed or stopped.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Temporal explicitly describes cooperative activity cancellation and timeout/retry semantics; ExoFlow states conditions for repeated execution and external output.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Use stable operation identities, scoped effect control and reconciliation; represent uncertainty rather than invent success/failure.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Unqualified exactly-once claims are rejected; scoped recovery systems remain legitimate.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: An uncooperative external system may make immediate resolution impossible.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Compensation may be non-equivalent, impossible or itself faulty; a stopped workflow can still owe a remedy.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Sagas §6 discusses errors including failed compensation; exception patterns distinguish recovery actions.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Treat compensation as fallible work with its own preconditions and residual-obligation disposition.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Universal world restoration is rejected. Closure accounting is synthesised from the surviving distinctions, not attributed as a historical theorem.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Who may waive or transfer an unresolved obligation depends on the actual relationship.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Locally correct participants can deadlock globally; successful sending does not establish acceptance or commitment.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The interorganisational paper gives a model-level compatibility problem; BPEL correlation and ActionWorkflow commitment distinctions address different boundaries.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Check shared protocol meaning/order and retain participant authority boundaries alongside local enactment.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Global guarantees are assumption-sensitive; neither central visibility nor a choreography diagram is enough.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Open strategic or changing partners exceed the inspected closed-model assumptions.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Standard compliance and model interchange do not guarantee executable semantic support, and upgrades can regress.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The historical Bamberg benchmark uses isolated expected-trace tests on three engines/four versions each, finding incomplete support and regressions.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Test the used subset/version and declare the portability layer. Do not turn the old benchmark into a present-day product ranking.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Conformance badges and feature counts are not adequate correctness or adoption criteria. The authors’ market-success inference is not accepted as proof of unimportant omissions.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Finite tests cover neither all combinations nor today’s versions; no current independent universal benchmark is claimed.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Durable execution exposes determinism, persistence and external-effect assumptions; performance optimisations do not remove them.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Temporal/Microsoft documentation and ExoFlow’s declared task conditions were inspected; DSE’s controlled speculative-recovery boundary and experimental setup were read.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Keep replay-sensitive code within contract, preserve sufficient state and account for external actions; choose another persistence model when appropriate.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Deterministic replay is domain-specific rather than the definition of workflow management; scoped exactly-once remains valid under assumptions.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Correct annotations, external cooperation and version compatibility require implementation evidence.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A sound new definition and valid new code are not sufficient for a partially completed old instance.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: ADEPTflex examines schema/state transformations; declarative changes and Microsoft replay constraints expose related but distinct continuity questions.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Choose checked state migration, coexistence, pinning or consciously adjudicated restart, with pending interactions accounted for.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: The definition-only candidate EWM-067 is superseded by EWM-048. No migration is imposed where coexistence is adequate.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Business-obligation changes may remain invalid even after a model-valid state mapping.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: More flexible models can contain conflicting constraints or demand more understanding from workers than a route does.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Declare’s automata-based checks identify conflicts/dead activities and distinguish temporary obligations; comparative user comprehension is not established here.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Use constraints for genuine variation, prescribed fragments for stable work and participant-informed explanations.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Flexibility is a set of conditional alternatives, not a maturity ranking or universal replacement.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: The comparative burden on users and maintainers requires actual task evidence.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Case/stage completion does not necessarily mean every required child achieved a successful result.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: CMMN 1.1 §8.6.1 was inspected visually: permitted states for relevant children include Disabled, Completed, Terminated and Failed, while active work constrains completion.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Distinguish normative lifecycle completion from the organisation’s acceptance and result predicates.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: A universal all-children-succeeded rule would misrepresent the standard; a separate outcome claim is needed where relevant.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: The legitimate meaning of closure under failed/disabled work is context-specific.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Contextual rule extension can accumulate opaque exception precedence or select a superficially fitting but inappropriate variant.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Worklets supplies a concrete ripple-down selection/replacement mechanism; general maintenance and outcome costs are not independently measured in the inspected paper.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Preserve rule rationale and parent interface constraints, and choose direct human selection when reuse does not pay.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Worklets remain conditional; the rule-accumulation objection is partly analytical rather than an invented reported incident.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: When accumulated exceptions should trigger general redesign remains a contextual question.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Logs omit work, event labels can mislead, and conformance/monitoring metrics can reward the wrong behaviour.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The audit specification limits its event scope; conformance uses case/activity/order abstractions; reported fault categories in the PanDA presentation can overlap.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Treat observations as evidence for an explicit consumer and permit competing explanations before intervention.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Universal log truth is rejected; monitoring is classified as useful but easily gamed.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: External observation and incentives may be unavailable or costly to assess.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Re-executable workflows and complete metadata do not necessarily reproduce or justify a scientific result.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Yevis explicitly excludes expected-output verification; Taverna describes provenance and dependencies. The 2012 decay abstract and 2024 record do not supply inspected numerical results.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Declare reproducibility level, dependency context and appropriate scientific output oracle rather than equating exit success with validity.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Scientific provenance is retained as domain-specific support, not a guarantee of scientific truth.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Decay rates and later replication findings from inaccessible full texts are not inferred.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Fault frequency does not equal resource impact, and telemetry sample selection limits generalisation.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The 2025 slides report 50 million programs/12% faults, focus further on site-monitoring reports and selected sites, and distinguish reported sources. Slides are not full methods.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Keep unit, observation boundary and selection visible; prioritise with actual consequence/cost rather than frequency alone.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: No worldwide workflow failure rate or proved mitigation benefit is derived. Recent operational evidence nevertheless reinforces resource/data/environment limits.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Exact observation window, complete denominator construction and causal root-cause validation were unavailable.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Static public low-code/agent templates are not executions and may hide custom or external controls.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The n8n preprint analyses more than 6,000 templates, distinguishes execution/configuration edges and acknowledges public selection and hidden behaviour threats.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Use static findings to formulate targeted runtime questions, not incident frequencies or universal architecture verdicts.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Low-code and agent conclusions remain conditional; autonomous effectiveness remains unresolved.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Actual runtime failures, user costs and off-template mechanisms need independent evidence.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Pinning a semantic environment and declaring compatibility do not establish that the outputs or compatibility judgement are correct.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The 2026 semantic-isolation proposal’s audit yields four exposure-positive cases among 54 durable ones in a selected top-100 population; exposure is not an incident. Controlled prototype graphs also demonstrate four anomalies and their prevention: both static pinning and SSI work for the tested closed dependency set, while online extension handles the demonstrated discovery case.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Keep environment identity and compatibility as explicit assumptions, require a suitable outcome evaluation and disallow self-authorising acceptance. Prefer closed-world pinning when sufficient; the extra dynamic mechanism needs a late-discovery trigger. The source leaves stronger shared-write/visible-effect serialisability to future work.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: EWM-073 is assumption-sensitive and EWM-074 unresolved, not promoted to a mature general doctrine.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Unreplicated preprint/prototype evidence cannot establish long-term robustness or general economic benefit.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Having a non-recursive escape path does not alone ensure that every execution eventually takes it.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The revised pattern report p.44 contains stronger eventual-completion wording. Analytical counterexample: repeatedly select recursive A while the base branch D remains available.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Add a decreasing measure, bound or relevant execution/fairness condition when inevitable completion is required; otherwise claim only an available completion path.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: EWM-011 explicitly narrows the prose claim and EWM-016 preserves the distinction between existential completion and inevitability.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Actual termination reasoning depends on data and selection policy, not only graph shape.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Indefinite event retention is neither automatically sufficient nor always necessary for recovery and accountability.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The WfMC audit specification leaves archiving outside its scope; replay requires relevant history, while semantic drift can make retained records insufficient for stronger claims.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Declare required consumers, reconstruction claims and retirement conditions, preserving necessary operation keys and dependencies.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: EWM-072 is rejected; EWM-046 retains claim-relative sufficiency without setting legal durations.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Actual retention and privacy obligations are outside this neutral technical study.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Locally improving a metric or generating a valid-looking workflow does not establish safe general self-revision.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Inspected current evidence is static/proposal/prototype evidence, while established change and observation work exposes continuity and outcome obligations.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Use explicit authorised objectives, bounded proposals, independent-of-proposal evaluation and continuity checks; allow experiments without asserting a general guarantee.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS_AND_PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: General safe autonomous optimisation remains researched but unresolved; it is not a retained unconditional control.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Prospective cross-setting comparative evidence and robust evaluation of changed obligations are still needed.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Prescription costs exceptions; discretion costs explanation and consistent constraint enforcement.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Stable repeated work with known dependencies and high consequence of omission.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Cases whose next valid action depends on information not yet available.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Prescribed routine fragments with explicit case/constraint boundaries and a repair path.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Nominal discretion that silently bypasses constraints, or a rigid model with hidden manual work.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Can meaningful alternatives be specified without prohibitive branching, and can workers explain a permissible next action?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: No universal crossover threshold or comparative comprehension effect is established.

internal_tensions.COSTS: General joins, reset arcs and unbounded state increase analysis cost; restrictions can distort the work.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: A restricted/structured model expresses every consequential case.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Real loops, cancellations or unstructured dependencies would be lost by restriction.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Restricted core plus explicitly delimited exceptional submodels and appropriate bounded analysis.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: The exception interface violates the assumptions of the core proof.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Which required counterexample cannot be expressed or verified in the simpler model?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Finite tests and abstractions may not cover all interactions.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Global information helps diagnosis but may expose private state and imply unavailable control.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: One accountable organisation actually controls the relevant resources and actions.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Independent participants retain private policies and external authority.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Local orchestration with agreed public message/commitment contracts.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: A global model silently assumes internal details or cooperation absent from local contracts.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: What is the minimum public behaviour necessary to establish the shared coordination claim?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Open strategic participation exceeds inspected formal models.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Waiting and manual repair cost time; blind retry/compensation can cause duplicate or irreversible damage.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Stable operation keys and cooperative idempotent/transactional participants make repetition safe.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Opaque or irreversible effects cannot be queried or safely repeated.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Automatic recovery inside a verified boundary, explicit adjudication at ambiguous external edges.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: An internal timeout is treated as evidence about an outside commit.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Does the recovery mechanism have evidence or a protocol covering each possibly repeated effect?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Some outcomes may remain permanently uncertain.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Change/rule accretion burdens operators; freezing may make legitimate work impossible.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Instances are short-lived and old semantics remain acceptable.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Changed obligations or case information make the old route unusable.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Version coexistence plus checked migration for cases that actually need it; selective worklet reuse.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Current state or pending messages do not fit the new version despite a sound target.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Can existing cases complete acceptably without migration, and what exact state transformation would be required?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Business validity can remain outside formal migration proofs.

internal_tensions.COSTS: More history costs storage/interpretation and may expose unnecessary data; less history can break recovery.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Long retry, review or scientific reproducibility claims need the retained facts.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Consumers and obligations have expired or a sufficient compact representation exists.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Snapshots plus required provenance and operation references, with a tested retirement rule.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Compaction removes deduplication or migration facts still needed by a late event.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Which future legitimate claim fails without each retained record?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Legal and domain-specific retention duties are not determined here.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Priority optimisation may starve cases or overload staff; strict equality may waste scarce expertise.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Urgent, high-consequence or strongly constrained tasks have a justified precedence.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Workload distribution and starvation undermine service or participation.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Explicit priority classes, constrained assignment and review of waiting/overload evidence.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Metrics improve while hidden work or the least powerful participants bear increased costs.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Who waits longer or works harder under the policy, and is that distribution justified?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Fairness has no universal metric in the inspected corpus.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Independent observation can be intrusive and costly; unexamined declarations can conceal failure.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: High-consequence or disputed results make unsupported declaration inadequate.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Low-consequence trusted work and directly accountable participants make reports sufficient.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Claim-relative evidence and selective checks, with explicit acceptance meaning.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: The check merely repeats the same source, or formal acceptance masks coercion.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: What error would this extra observation detect that the existing evidence would miss?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Suitable observation and consent require the actual setting.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Portable subsets may be weak; extensions increase exit and testing costs.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Switching/interoperability risk is concrete and the shared subset is adequate.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Specialised constructs offer demonstrated value exceeding the cost of dependency.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Use a tested portable core and explicit versioned adapters for justified extensions.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Exported diagrams conceal non-exported code, data semantics or history constraints.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Can required behaviour and in-flight state actually move at an acceptable cost?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Historical conformance studies do not rank current offerings.

internal_tensions.COSTS: Pinning preserves context but can retain defects; updates can invalidate old decisions.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Reproducibility or long-lived commitments depend on a stable environment.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: New evidence or defects make the old environment unacceptable.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Bounded reviewed updates with explicit compatibility and current-instance adjudication.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: The same optimiser authors both the change and the sole evidence that it is safe.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: What externally assessable consequence test would reject an incompatible update?
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Current preprints do not establish a generally reliable semantic compatibility oracle.

empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.UNITS: Organisations, intended/enacted processes and validated simulation comparisons; denominators are not interchangeable.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.SAMPLE: 10 Dutch organisations and 25 intended processes; 5 implementing organisations and 7 enacted processes; 5 validated simulation comparisons after 2 exclusions.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.SETTING: 2001–2012 longitudinal programme, final article published 2016; historical organisational deployment.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.COMPARISON: Before/after observations and calibrated simulation, not random assignment.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.MEASURES: Deployment continuation/abandonment, process lead time and service-time effects discussed in the study.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.OUTCOMES_SUPPORTED: Most evaluated implementations show favourable adjusted performance, with a material HRM lead/waiting-time exception. Abandonment remains part of adoption evidence but is primarily attributed to organisational/programme changes, not technical workflow-engine failure.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Selected participating organisations, attrition, management recall, simulation assumptions and two unusable process models/logs constrain causal and external validity. No pooled effect estimate exported.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.INDEPENDENCE: Earlier preliminary publications describe this programme and are not independent replications.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.USE_IN_THIS_PACKET: EWM-004/058/063/071: require contextual payoff evidence and retain failure cases in the denominator.

empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.UNITS: Executable feature tests and engine/version combinations.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.SAMPLE: 3 engines, 4 versions each; the historical test suite reports 38 constructs and 113 features.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.SETTING: BPMN 2.0 engine implementations tested for the 2016 paper.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.COMPARISON: Expected versus observed execution traces and differences between versions.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.MEASURES: Successful feature execution, missing support and regressions.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.OUTCOMES_SUPPORTED: Standard support can be incomplete and regress between versions; semantic correspondence needs actual testing.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Isolated tests do not establish all real process interactions; historical products/versions are not current rankings. Market success is not an empirical demonstration that missing features are harmless.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.INDEPENDENCE: One benchmark programme, not twelve independent industrial deployment studies.
empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.USE_IN_THIS_PACKET: EWM-018/041/061/066: reject syntax/brand as sufficient assurance.

empirical_and_case_evidence_cards.UNITS: Work practice in a ward and participatory design activity.

formal_evidence_cards.NAME: Classical workflow-net soundness
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL: Ordinary workflow net with designated source/sink and specified initial/final markings.
formal_evidence_cards.GUARANTEE: Every reachable marking permits a completion path; reaching the final place means proper completion without residual tokens; every task is potentially executable.
formal_evidence_cards.ASSUMPTIONS: Exact net class and token/case interpretation; the short-circuit characterisation is used only within its theorem conditions.
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATIONS: Show that the actual model has the required structure and that the engine subset realises its semantics.
formal_evidence_cards.DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: Inevitable termination of every execution, fairness, resource availability, deadlines, data validity or business success.

formal_evidence_cards.NAME: Variants, cancellation and decidability
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL: Specified variants of soundness, extended nets and YAWL control semantics.
formal_evidence_cards.GUARANTEE: Results distinguish which behavioural predicates are decidable or compositional in which model classes.
formal_evidence_cards.ASSUMPTIONS: Classical, k-sound, generalised, weak/relaxed or other predicates are not conflated; reset and OR-join extensions retain their particular restrictions.
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATIONS: Select the predicate and check every transformation/reduction or composition assumption.
formal_evidence_cards.DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: That every engine is unanalysable because one unrestricted model is undecidable, or that a theorem for ordinary nets covers every cancellation model.

formal_evidence_cards.NAME: Dynamic change
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL: The ADEPTflex graph, state and data model with specified change operations.
formal_evidence_cards.GUARANTEE: Admissible transformations preserve the properties established under the operation-specific preconditions.
formal_evidence_cards.ASSUMPTIONS: Current execution state, data dependencies and permitted operations are known.
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATIONS: Supply a valid mapping for the actual live instance and its outstanding work; external effects may require an additional interface obligation.
formal_evidence_cards.DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: Safe arbitrary migration merely because the target definition is sound.

formal_evidence_cards.NAME: Declarative verification
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL: Constraint/trace models and associated verification representation used by the paper.
formal_evidence_cards.GUARANTEE: Conflicts, dead activities and selected consistency/progress issues can be detected within the declared constraint semantics.
formal_evidence_cards.ASSUMPTIONS: Finite-completion interpretation and temporal/activation semantics are explicit.
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATIONS: The implemented rule set must match the analysed model; pending obligations and end conditions must be interpreted correctly.
formal_evidence_cards.DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: That any locally permitted next action eventually completes all obligations, or that people necessarily understand dense constraint sets.

formal_evidence_cards.NAME: Inter-organisational composition
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL: Loosely coupled local workflow-net models with explicit interaction places/relations.
formal_evidence_cards.GUARANTEE: Compatibility/completion analysis considers the coupled model rather than local correctness alone.
formal_evidence_cards.ASSUMPTIONS: The assumed communication and participant behaviour matches the model.
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATIONS: Check contracts, correlation and private/local assumptions at the actual interface.
formal_evidence_cards.DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: Agreement of autonomous participants, reliable arbitrary networks or progress under adversarial behaviour outside the model.

formal_evidence_cards.NAME: Workflow satisfiability
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL: Step/user authorisations and user-independent assignment constraints under the paper’s parameterised formulation.
formal_evidence_cards.GUARANTEE: Feasible assignments can be found/ruled out under the studied constraint class and algorithm assumptions.
formal_evidence_cards.ASSUMPTIONS: Time ordering is outside the inspected problem formulation; specific constraint classes matter.
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATIONS: Translate real authorisation/duty rules faithfully and separately establish capacity/time feasibility.
formal_evidence_cards.DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: Available workers, humane workloads, fair assignments, an executable calendar or authority to waive a requirement.

formal_evidence_cards.NAME: Scoped exactly-once DAG recovery
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL: ExoFlow DAG execution under its task/rollback and persistence model.
formal_evidence_cards.GUARANTEE: Exactly-once recovery semantics are established for the declared cooperative boundary, not for unconstrained outside effects.
formal_evidence_cards.ASSUMPTIONS: Determinism and idempotent tasks or idempotent rollback; appropriate persistent state before external output; version-specific limitations.
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATIONS: Validate application annotations and external-effect placement; do not silently add unavailable cross-task transactions.
formal_evidence_cards.DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: Universal exactly-once business/physical outcomes, or a general impossibility of valid scoped exactly-once guarantees.

formal_evidence_cards.NAME: Replay and semantic compatibility
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL: Replay-based orchestration implementations; a separate 2026 proposed semantic-environment contract.
formal_evidence_cards.GUARANTEE: Implementation replay requires compatible command generation; proposed semantic isolation constrains declared compatibility, not arbitrary truth.
formal_evidence_cards.ASSUMPTIONS: Deterministic orchestrator code and compatible history; for the proposal, an adequate semantic dependency and compatibility specification.
formal_evidence_cards.MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATIONS: Keep nondeterministic effects outside replayed local code and evaluate semantic assumptions separately from replay compatibility.
formal_evidence_cards.DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: A universal theorem covering all durable engines or a guarantee that a declared compatibility predicate is correct.

analytical_tests.NAME: Parallel join with a cancelled branch
analytical_tests.CASE: A split activates A and B. A completes, B is cancelled before arrival at a join.
analytical_tests.COMPOSED_EXPECTATION: Do not insert a fictional success token or wait blindly. Determine the specified join/cancellation semantics, remaining branch membership and completion scope. The model may require handler-driven withdrawal, a different join policy or an explicitly unresolved case.
analytical_tests.LIMIT: This identifies a semantic obligation, not a claim that every AND-join must continue after cancellation.

analytical_tests.NAME: Sound net, unavailable worker
analytical_tests.CASE: An ordinary sound net has one task whose only authorised performer is indefinitely absent.
analytical_tests.COMPOSED_EXPECTATION: Retain the soundness result for its resource-free model, but deny an inference of actual completion. Check substitution, capacity, escalation or a valid decision to wait.
analytical_tests.LIMIT: No invented service-time estimate or unfairness frequency is attached.

analytical_tests.NAME: Timed-out activity already committed
analytical_tests.CASE: A remote payment commits, but its reply is lost and the workflow sees a timeout.
analytical_tests.COMPOSED_EXPECTATION: Treat effect as uncertain. Reuse a valid idempotency key or query/reconcile under the real contract; do not unconditionally issue a fresh payment or assume cancellation undoes it.
analytical_tests.LIMIT: The example is analytical and does not assert any payment product behaviour.

analytical_tests.NAME: Halfway migration into a changed process
analytical_tests.CASE: An old instance completed A, started B and sent an external request; the new sound model removes B and expects a different data field.
analytical_tests.COMPOSED_EXPECTATION: Soundness of the new definition is insufficient. Check control/data mapping, current worker and external request disposition; select migration, coexistence, quiescence or authorised repair with retained references.
analytical_tests.LIMIT: No universal migration operator is invented.

analytical_tests.NAME: Human completion without intended effect
analytical_tests.CASE: A worker clicks complete after preparing a shipment label, but the parcel is not dispatched.
analytical_tests.COMPOSED_EXPECTATION: Interpret the click as the declaration supported by its evidence. If the case promise includes dispatch, require proportionate relevant confirmation or explicit qualified acceptance; do not demand surveillance as the only remedy.
analytical_tests.LIMIT: The correct evidence standard depends on the declared promise and harm, not a universal physical sensor.

analytical_tests.NAME: Valid next case action cannot be predetermined
analytical_tests.CASE: A complex case can require additional investigation, consultation or closure depending on newly learned facts.
analytical_tests.COMPOSED_EXPECTATION: Use case data and authorised discretion with identifiable constraints and completion criteria. A fixed route is not mandatory; declarative or worklet support is optional when it protects a real invariant.
analytical_tests.LIMIT: This is a selection argument, not proof that case management always outperforms prescribed workflow.

analytical_tests.NAME: Favourable structured example
analytical_tests.CASE: Repeated requests have stable eligibility data, two known concurrent checks and an observable acceptance result.
analytical_tests.COMPOSED_EXPECTATION: A small executable subset, tested join, clear ownership and an effect consumer form a coherent engine use case. Add durable recovery only if losing the in-flight state has a material consequence.
analytical_tests.LIMIT: Plausible operation is not empirical cost-benefit validation.

analytical_tests.NAME: Non-trigger minimal procedure
